shared_elements: low-relief animals in profile on a monolithic pillar face
quadruped with legs shown in profile
sinuous snake-like or curving band forms in the lower zone
horizontal band separating zones of carving
pillar treated as a body with carving wrapping the sides
justification: Both surfaces present a vertical monolithic pillar carved in shallow, flat, schematic low relief with repeated profile animals set in registers and sinuous snake-like curves occupying the lower zone, a fairly specific combination for an anthropomorphic-pillar format. The clearest difference is that B renders an explicit human head with brow, nose and jaw and organises its figures in vertical columns down the sides, whereas A's carvings are laid out in strict horizontal rows (a file of birds over a band over quadrupeds) with no facial features shown.
